body:
Five design fixes the maintainer found on a device after 3.2.0.

1. **Overview account heading on one line.** With several accounts the section heading shows the
   email and, under it, the server URL. Make it "email  ·  server" on ONE line, breaking into two
   lines only when it does not fit the width (Compose: a Row/FlowRow that wraps, or measure and
   fall back; the server part in the muted style as today). Android only (the web has no sections).
2. **That heading slim.** As little vertical space as possible: one text line where it fits, small
   top padding to separate it from the previous section's last card, no extra bottom padding.
3. **Server admin from the main menu, per account.** The drawer's "Server admin" entry opens the
   first signed-in admin account. With several admin accounts it must open a chooser listing them
   (email · server), with one it opens that account's console directly; keep the console's app bar
   naming the server. Remove the "Server admin" button from the Account screen (the maintainer
   does not want it there). Strings: a chooser title, nine locales.
4. **Reorder accounts by drag.** The Accounts screen reorders with up/down arrows; List properties
   reorders categories by dragging a handle (T-30, ListPropsScreen.kt ~line 424). Use the same
   mechanism for accounts: extract the drag-reorder into a shared composable (e.g. ui/DragReorder.kt)
   used by both, keep the category behaviour pixel-identical, and let the server accounts be dragged
   among themselves while the local area stays last and cannot be dragged. Arrows go.
5. **New list without a name says why.** Creating a list with a blank name silently does nothing
   on Android; the web shows the browser's native "required" bubble. On both clients: the name
   field goes into its error state with the inline message "Enter a name." (nine locales each,
   identical English so crossClient pairs them); the error clears when the user types. Same for a
   blank currency on a new ledger on Android (today it also returns silently): "Enter a currency."
   — check what the web does there and match. On the web drop `required` on that field in favour of
   the inline message so both clients behave the same (keep the field required semantically).
title: Android UI after 3.2.0: one-line slim account headings, server-admin chooser per account, drag-reorder accounts, new-list name validation (both clients)
